topic: Recovery evidence for reducing Qwen3-0.6B from eight to four unique KV heads

one_shot_head_averaging.reason: Mean pooling is the best simple checkpoint initializer in the original GQA study, but that recipe includes additional pre-training. A decoder-only LLaMA2 study measured catastrophic perplexity after mean-pool initialization, while activation-aware initialization plus LoRA recovered much of the loss. No primary source tests zero-shot Qwen3-0.6B GQA-8 to GQA-4 conversion.

reported_recovery_budgets.other: About 600 TPUv3 chip-days at alpha=0.05 for T5 XXL
reported_recovery_budgets.note: The paper does not report an exact token count for this run.

reported_recovery_budgets.budget: 23,000 FLANv2 samples for activation-aware initialization; 23,000 to 232,000 FLANv2 samples for one-epoch LoRA ablations
reported_recovery_budgets.other: The main LLaMA2 run used 232,000 samples, LoRA, and a constant 4e-5 learning rate
reported_recovery_budgets.note: Samples are not tokens and their sequence-length distribution is not reported, so a token budget cannot be reconstructed.

reported_recovery_budgets.budget: 0.2B tokens for fusion, 1B tokens for the early comparison, and up to 50B tokens for continued pre-training
reported_recovery_budgets.other: The abstract reports 0.25% of original pre-training budget; the paper also labels 0.5B and 1B runs as about 0.01% and 0.05%
reported_recovery_budgets.note: The paper states LLaMA2 used 2T pre-training tokens, making 50B equal to 2.5%, not 0.25%, and 0.5B equal to 0.025%, not 0.01%. Treat its percentage labels as internally inconsistent and prefer the absolute token counts.

reported_recovery_budgets.budget: 262,144 C4 calibration tokens plus 93M pruning-training tokens for LLaMA2-7B 32-to-16 KV-head conversion
reported_recovery_budgets.other: Eight A100 GPUs were used for teacher SFT and pruning training
reported_recovery_budgets.note: This is exact token accounting for an MHA-to-GQA experiment, not Qwen GQA-to-GQA recovery.

qwen_scale_projection.note: Applying the GQA paper's 5% fraction to the Qwen3 family's approximately 36T-token corpus gives 1.8T tokens. No source establishes that Qwen3-0.6B needs or would recover with this amount.

derived_for_eight_to_four_unique_kv_head.derivation: 28 layers * 2 cache tensors * KV heads * 128 dimensions * 2 BF16 bytes

recommended_local_experiment.name: gradual_teacher_distilled_gqa8_to_gqa4_recovery_screen
recommended_local_experiment.purpose: Test whether the exact full-model four-head structure is locally recoverable enough to justify a larger training run; do not claim final model quality or cost reduction.
recommended_local_experiment.why_this_experiment: It combines the least expensive transferable findings: use activation behavior rather than weight distance for grouping, avoid an abrupt mean-pooling cliff with a gradual original-to-shared-head gate, and adapt a small tied parameter set against the original model's logits.

data.calibration: First 4,096 non-empty Qwen tokens from the cached WikiText-2 train split, deterministic sequential order
data.training: Next 8,192 non-overlapping Qwen tokens from the cached WikiText-2 train split, sequence length 128, microbatch 1, 64 optimizer steps
data.confirmation_holdout: Existing deterministic sequential 4,096-target-token WikiText-2 test fixture, run only after the first holdout passes
data.teacher: Unmodified pinned Qwen3-0.6B checkpoint with teacher logits precomputed for the fixed training tokens

arms.description: Current minimum joint K/V weight-distance pairing and hard pair mean across all 28 layers, with no adaptation.
Choose each layer's joint K/V perfect pairing by minimum calibration-set distance between post-QK-normalization, pre-RoPE activations; apply the same hard pair mean with no adaptation.

Use the activation-aware pairs. Initialize four shared K and V projections per layer by pair means. During training blend each original branch and its shared branch with a scalar gate z, linearly anneal z from 1 to 0 over steps 1-48, and keep z=0 for steps 49-64. Remove original branches before evaluation.

trainable_parameters.shared_kv_projections: Four tied K heads and four tied V heads in every layer
trainable_parameters.lora: Rank-8 LoRA on q_proj and o_proj only; merge adapters before evaluation
trainable_parameters.frozen: Embedding, norms, MLP, language head, and every other base parameter
trainable_parameters.constraint: No independently trainable duplicate K/V branch may remain after z reaches zero

optimization.loss: 0.7 * teacher-logit KL at temperature 2 + 0.3 * next-token cross entropy
optimization.precision: BF16 model weights with FP32 optimizer state

decision_rule.positive_recoverability_signal: Held-out NLL improves monotonically at 2K, 4K, and 8K tokens and the 8K candidate passes every existing 512-token quality gate; then require confirmation on the untouched 4,096-token fixture.
decision_rule.negative_result: Reject this recovery path if NLL is non-monotonic after 4K tokens or the 8K candidate remains outside any existing gate by more than 2x its allowed regression.
decision_rule.claim_if_negative: This exact gradual tied-head adaptation is not promising at the tested budget; it does not disprove recovery at the literature's much larger budgets.

cpu_feasibility_notes: The screen uses 8,192 training tokens rather than the literature's 23K variable-length samples, 93M tokens, 0.2B tokens, or 5% pre-training budget.
Teacher logits are precomputed and only the tied structural parameters plus small adapters receive gradients.
This is deliberately a trend and gate test; its budget is far too small to validate production recovery.

sources.title: GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints
direct_claim_paraphrases: Checkpoint conversion mean-pools K and V heads within each target group, and mean pooling performed better than selecting one head or random initialization.
The converted checkpoint is then trained for a fraction alpha of its original pre-training steps; the main alpha=0.05 run used 5% of original compute and about 600 TPUv3 chip-days.
GQA had reasonable performance immediately after conversion, whereas MQA required uptraining; both benefited at 5%, with diminishing returns at 10%.
Reducing H KV heads to one reduces KV-cache capacity and KV data loading by a factor of H.
scope_limits: T5 encoder-decoder checkpoints, not a decoder-only Qwen model
MHA-to-GQA/MQA, not an already-GQA eight-to-four conversion
No QK normalization
The paper explicitly lists decoder-only evaluation as future work

sources.title: Effectively Compress KV Heads for LLM
direct_claim_paraphrases: On LLaMA2-7B compressed from 32 to 16 KV heads, mean-pool initialization collapsed to WikiText-2 perplexity 1079.43 and C4 perplexity 625.68; its reported fine-tuned perplexities remained the same.
Activation-SVD initialization for the same 50% head reduction started at perplexity 13.57/18.57 and reached 7.08/9.12 after LoRA, versus the uncompressed model's 5.47/6.98.
The activation-aware initializer used 23K FLANv2 samples; increasing initialization data to 232K did not help, while larger fine-tuning sets generally improved recovery.
With only 23K fine-tuning samples, the 50%-head candidate reached perplexity 7.29/9.41 and average commonsense QA 61.93 versus 62.50 for the uncompressed model.
At context length 2048 on one 80GB A100, measured decode throughput rose from 8.05 to 13.41 tokens/s for the 50%-head LLaMA2-7B candidate.
scope_limits: ArXiv preprint rather than a reported peer-reviewed venue
LLaMA2 MHA-to-GQA, not Qwen GQA-to-GQA
FLANv2 counts are samples, not tokens
Its RoPE key-cache path cannot always be folded into standard GQA weights and can add prefill overhead
It does not test Qwen's QK normalization
Single-device token throughput is not serving cost or SLO evidence

sources.title: DHA: Learning Decoupled-Head Attention from Transformer Checkpoints via Adaptive Heads Fusion
direct_claim_paraphrases: DHA replaces abrupt averaging with search, progressive linear head fusion, and continued pre-training.
The reported fusion phase used 0.2B tokens; early and extended continued-pretraining comparisons used 1B and up to 50B tokens.
The paper reports that 0.2B-token DHA matched the performance reached by GQA at 1B tokens in one comparison.
It proposes converting an existing GQA checkpoint by first losslessly replicating KV heads into MHA form or by grouping existing GQA KV heads before fusion.
It finds layer and K-versus-V redundancy varies, motivating non-uniform and separately allocated K/V head budgets.
scope_limits: Experiments are on LLaMA2 and Sheared-LLaMA MHA checkpoints
GQA-to-DHA compatibility is proposed but not experimentally validated in the paper
Reported percentage budgets are internally inconsistent with its own absolute token counts
The architecture is not standard uniform GQA and needs a compatible runtime

sources.title: Align Attention Heads Before Merging Them: An Effective Way for Converting MHA to GQA
direct_claim_paraphrases: The method calibrates on 128 C4 sequences of 2048 tokens, aligns heads with output-preserving Procrustes transforms, then gradually transfers original heads into new shared heads with L0 masks and teacher-logit distillation.
Its LLaMA2-7B 32-to-16 conversion used 93M pruning-training tokens after a 37.2M-token teacher SFT run.
The pruning path initializes masks at the original heads and constrains them toward the shared heads instead of beginning from a fully collapsed hard merge.
The paper gives a RoPE-compatible constrained rotation for key/query heads.
scope_limits: MHA-to-GQA on LLaMA2 and Sheared-LLaMA, not Qwen GQA-to-GQA
Eight A100 GPUs were used for training
No test of QK normalization
Task-supervised recovery may not preserve broad agent behavior

sources.title: Qwen3: Think Deeper, Act Faster
direct_claim_paraphrases: Qwen3-0.6B has 28 layers, 16 query heads, 8 KV heads, and a 32K context length.
The Qwen3 family used approximately 36T pre-training tokens.
Qwen3's 30B-A3B and 235B-A22B MoE models were designed with four KV heads, showing that four-head family architectures are viable when trained that way.
scope_limits: The 36T figure is family-level documentation, not an exact per-checkpoint training ledger
Four KV heads in separately trained MoE models do not show that the dense 0.6B checkpoint can be converted

sources.title: Qwen3-0.6B pinned config.json
direct_claim_paraphrases: The pinned checkpoint declares 28 layers, 16 attention heads, 8 KV heads, head dimension 128, BF16 dtype, and cache use enabled.
scope_limits: Configuration geometry alone provides no recovery, kernel, throughput, or cost evidence

defensible: Exactly 50% less semantic BF16 KV storage per token for eight-to-four unique heads
Exactly 50% less semantic KV data to read in an attention implementation that loads only the four unique heads
Up to 2x KV-limited sequence capacity before allocator and workspace overhead
1.75 GiB saved per 32K sequence and 112 GiB saved at 64 simultaneous 32K sequences
About 4.93% lower checkpoint weight bytes if duplicate K/V projection storage is physically eliminated
material_gain_if_quality_and_runtime_are.analog_only: A decoder-only LLaMA2 experiment measured 1.67x decode throughput at 50% KV-head reduction and context 2048, but this is not transferable as a Qwen serving or cost claim.
material_gain_if_quality_and_runtime_are.cost_conclusion: No defensible percent reduction in total dollars per token exists yet. The gain can approach a device-count or concurrency discontinuity only when KV capacity or KV bandwidth is the binding resource; it can be negligible when weights, compute, prefill, or serving overhead dominate.

unsupported_claims: One-shot pair averaging is always unrecoverable
Eight-to-four Qwen3-0.6B recovery will succeed with 8,192 local training tokens
Five percent of Qwen's documented 36T tokens is necessary or sufficient
Activation-SVD or Procrustes transformations remain output-preserving through Qwen3 QK normalization without a new derivation
A four-head architecture used by other Qwen3 family members proves this checkpoint can be converted
The custom alias attention kernel is correct, faster, or physically stores only unique heads
A 50% semantic KV reduction produces a 50% total inference-cost reduction
Teacher-forced WikiText quality predicts chat, reasoning, tool use, or end-to-end agent success
Any recovered model preserves safety or alignment behavior
